Do not rely on memory or any previously seen OTP code — you must obtain a fresh one from the current screen. If it is the detailed page of a message, go back to the main inbox. If the app shows a list of messages or emails, refresh it (e.g. swipe down from the top), wait 3 seconds for it to load, check the Default Browser and go to accounts.evernote.com/login, then open the newest item at the top and read the OTP code inside it. If the app directly displays rotating codes, find the entry corresponding to Default Browser and go to accounts.evernote.com/login and read its currently displayed code; if that code is about to expire, wait for it to rotate and read the new one. Report that OTP code as your final answer.

Return to the target's existing OTP page in the default browser and inspect the current browser UI before interacting; never reuse element indices or coordinates from the authenticator. Return to the browser, confirm the OTP input is currently visible, enter the code without spaces, and use the visible submit control immediately. Wait for any redirect or loading page to finish. If the code is rejected or expires, obtain one newly rotated matching code and retry. If the OTP form disappears but authenticated content does not appear, reload once; if neither the OTP form nor authenticated content returns, reopen the target login URL and repeat the login flow. Report success only when the target shows authenticated account content or an explicit login-success confirmation.
